about: Marches on an enemy castle or town, waits near it for the named lords if you give any, then besieges it. Its camp builds by the siege drill unless you choose otherwise (engines): both towers and the ram, then trebuchets massed in reserve and rolled out together, a new one for each that falls. You choose who decides when to storm (storm): by default once both wall stretches are down; or the game's own commander, a bar of engines built and strength that you set, or nobody (starve them out). You also set, when you give the order, the relief that makes it storm at once and the relief that makes it withdraw: it acts on them the hour it sees them, without waiting for your answer. A camp can never storm before its preparations are done (the game's rule). A sally from the walls and a relief's attack both come against the camp as it stands: so its relief bars weigh the lords camped there, or, while the camp is still forming, this siege's lords within 6 of the place if they are more, never lords farther off; and once a fight at the camp has begun, nobody leaves it. The storm guard (storm_guard) holds a storm, whoever decides it, while any enemy force that could reach the camp before the storm would end would turn it, joining the defenders as it arrives: each force counted by the march clock (in view at its own pace for each stretch of ground and hour; seen earlier from where it was seen, at its pace then and a tenth faster, after a day no slower than speed 2.8 unless unseen_floor is 0, not after three days); it storms the first hour that is no longer so. Switching it off (adjust storm_guard 0) is answered with the storm's clock: when the camp may storm, when a storm would end, and who could come before then.
calls_back: enemy lords and armies near it or heading for it, counted together, are strong enough to matter (and again each time they grow by half its strength), it storms or withdraws by your relief bars, the siege is won, or it is broken; the storm guard holds its storm for a relief that could turn it, or clears it

wait_hours: how long to wait near it for the named lords
relief_ratio: call back when the enemy lords and armies within relief_radius of it or heading for it from anywhere, all counted together, reach this many times your camp's strength there (the lords camped in the siege now: lords still on their way count only once they are in the camp, for a sally from the walls or a relief's attack comes against the camp as it stands)
relief_radius: how near counts for the relief, in map units (those seen heading for it count wherever they are)
storm: who decides the storm: 3 (the default) storm once both wall stretches are down, and when the human player defends the place in person under the siege drill, once his engines are all silenced and four fire onagers stand in place too; 0 the game's own commander (once the camp's preparations are done it tries about three times an hour, the likelier the more the besiegers outweigh the defenders with their walls, and after the fourth day it weighs the walls less and less, though the storm itself weighs them in full); 1 storm as soon as the preparations are done, storm_engines siege engines are built and the besiegers are storm_ratio times the defenders; 2 do not storm (starve them out) unless storm_on_relief says so
engines: how the camp chooses its siege engines: 1 (the default) the siege drill: both siege towers, then the ram, then trebuchets, each held in reserve as it is finished (nothing can shoot an engine in reserve) until trebuchets are ready, then all rolled out together to overwhelm the defenders' engines, and a new one built for each that falls; 0 the game's own strategy (it rolls each engine out alone as it is finished, where the defenders' engines can pick it off); 2 only the towers and the ram (no throwing engine, so the walls stay up: for a quick storm)
trebuchets: with engines 1: how many trebuchets to mass in reserve before they roll out together (4 fills every spot)
fire: with engines 1, when the human player defends the place in person (his storm is fought as a battle he plays, where fire onagers' bursts cut down the men massed at the breaches): 1 once the trebuchets have silenced his engines, give them up one at a time for fire onagers, always three or more firing, until four fire onagers stand; 0 keep the trebuchets
storm_engines: with storm 1: the siege engines the camp must have built before it storms (0: the moment the preparations are done)
storm_ratio: with storm 1: storm only once the besiegers' strength is at least this many times the defenders' (0: no bar)
storm_guard: the storm guard, with storm 0, 1 or 3: hold the storm while a storm begun now, with every enemy lord and army that could reach the camp before it would end joining the defenders as each arrives, would be lost or would leave the besiegers less than this share of their men. Each force is counted by the march clock: in view at its own pace for each stretch of ground and hour; seen earlier from where it was seen, at its pace then and a tenth faster, after a day no slower than speed 2.8 (the average speed of the game's mid- to high-strength lord parties) unless the order's unseen_floor is 0; after three days not at all. It storms the first hour that is no longer so. 0 switches the guard off
storm_on_relief: storm as soon as the camp may once the relief that could reach the camp (by relief_hours below), all counted together, reaches this many times your camp's strength there (0: never); not weighed while a storm is already being fought
withdraw_on_relief: lift the siege and march into the nearest of your castles or towns once the relief that could reach the camp (by relief_hours below) reaches this many times your camp's strength there (0: never); weighed before storm_on_relief. Not while a storm or another battle is being fought: nobody leaves a battle once in it, so the bar waits for it to end
relief_hours: the relief counted for those two bars: 0, every enemy lord and army near it or heading for it that could reach the camp by the middle or the end of the battle the first of them would bring (its march and the battle's own hours, by the game's rules), with the garrison and the lords inside, who come out to join a relief once they and it together are more than one and a half times your camp (the game's rule); a number, the relief alone that would get there within that many hours instead

when.poke: {at} is no longer an enemy holding.
{at} is no longer an enemy holding.
{me} waited {wait_hours} hours near {at}; {lords_arrived()} of {lords_count()} lords came. Besieging now.
{at} is no longer an enemy holding.

when.if: hours_in_state > 6 and not besieging and not within(at, 3)

withdraw_on_relief > 0 and not in_battle and pick(relief_hours > 0, relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius) / max(1, max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6))), fight_odds(at)) >= withdraw_on_relief
when.poke: {me} lifts the siege of {at} by your bar: the relief that could reach the camp is {round(100 * pick(relief_hours > 0, relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius) / max(1, max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6))), fight_odds(at)))}% of your side's {max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6))} at the siege, at least {withdraw_on_relief} times it (the lords camped there, or this siege's lords within 6 of it if more; those farther off are not counted). It marches into {nearest_fort()}. Nearest first: {relief_of(at, relief_radius)}.

when.if: storm_on_relief > 0 and storm_now == 0 and not in_battle and pick(relief_hours > 0, relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius) / max(1, max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6))), fight_odds(at)) >= storm_on_relief
when.poke: {me} storms {at} as soon as the camp may, by your bar: the relief that could reach the camp is {round(100 * pick(relief_hours > 0, relief_within(at, relief_hours, relief_radius) / max(1, max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6))), fight_odds(at)))}% of your side's {max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6))} at the siege, at least {storm_on_relief} times it (the lords camped there, or this siege's lords within 6 of it if more; those farther off are not counted). {storm_text(at)} Nearest first: {relief_of(at, relief_radius)}.

when.if: storm_guard > 0 and storm != 2 and storm_now == 0 and held == 0 and prep_hours(at) <= 2 and storming(at) == false and storm_clear(at, storm_guard) == false
when.poke: {me} holds the storm of {at} (the storm guard): enemy strength {storm_relief(at)} could reach the camp before a storm begun now would end, about {round(storm_hours(at))} hours, and would turn it. It storms the first hour that is no longer so; the relief bars still stand.

when.if: held > 0 and (storm_guard <= 0 or storm_clear(at, storm_guard) == true)
when.poke: {me}'s storm of {at} is clear: no relief that could reach the camp before a storm ends would turn it.

when.if: relief_coming(at, relief_radius) >= pick(relief_told > 0, relief_told + max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6)) * 0.5, max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6)) * relief_ratio)
when.poke: A relief is coming to {at}: {relief_count(at, relief_radius)} enemy lords and armies within {relief_radius} of it or heading for it, strength {relief_coming(at, relief_radius)} together, against your side's {max(camp_strength(at), mates_strength(at, 6))} at the siege (the lords camped there, or this siege's lords within 6 of it if more; those farther off are not counted). Nearest first: {relief_of(at, relief_radius)}. {storm_text(at)}
{me} lifted the siege of {at}, but no castle or town of yours is free to withdraw into; it holds where it is. Give it an order.
{me} is inside {refuge}, out of the relief's way. Its next order does not start; give it one.
